approaches.title: Blind stress-fabric alignment test across loaded bone sites
approaches.method: Scout intact, open micro-CT volumes for femoral head, vertebral body and calcaneus from at least two species, retaining only specimens for which defensible physiological boundary conditions can be fixed without viewing fabric orientation. Pre-register segmentation, mean-intercept-length fabric tensors in 5 mm-equivalent windows, linear-elastic finite elements, and the acute angle between the major fabric eigenvector and the nearest principal stress direction. Compare the observed median angle with 10,000 density-preserving random rotations and with a load-independent growth null fitted only to cortical shape and distance from surfaces; repeat over a predeclared ensemble of plausible load magnitudes without tuning directions.
steps: Scout and license-check at least three intact-bone datasets with metadata sufficient to define loads.
Freeze voxel-size, window-size, segmentation and finite-element convergence criteria before measuring alignment.
Compute specimen-level angular errors and null distributions with taxon and site as hierarchical effects.
Perform leave-one-site-out prediction and publish all meshes, load cases and randomization seeds.
approaches.decisive_result: For at least two of three sites, the pre-registered load case must yield a cross-specimen median angle at most 15 degrees and at least 10 degrees below both null medians, with a 95% hierarchical interval excluding zero; otherwise stress alignment is not supported at the stated tolerance.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than three usable paired geometry/load datasets, mesh non-convergence, or angular advantage under 10 degrees over either null shows that the approach cannot resolve the claim as stated.

references.note: Christen et al. 2014, Bone remodelling in humans is load-driven but not lazy

approaches.missing: Paired open whole-bone micro-CT and independently justified physiological load metadata may not exist for three sites; scouting must establish this before preregistration.

approaches.title: Out-of-sample load inference from trabecular architecture
approaches.method: Turn the potentially circular agreement test into a prediction task. For each scanned bone, define a finite library of anatomically plausible load directions before inspecting trabecular fabric. Fit a mechanostat-remodelling model and a load-independent reaction-diffusion growth model on training specimens, then ask each model to rank the held-out specimen's true load direction from architecture alone. Use the same density field and material law in both models, and score top-one identification plus angular error; this tests whether stress leaves information in architecture that a developmental null does not.
steps: Generate preregistered candidate load libraries and synthetic recovery tests.
Calibrate remodelling and developmental-null parameters only on training specimens.
Blind the held-out load label and rank candidate directions by posterior predictive discrepancy.
Repeat leave-one-specimen-out and report sensitivity to material anisotropy and boundary conditions.
approaches.decisive_result: Stress causation gains support if the remodelling model identifies the held-out load within 15 degrees in at least 80% of at least 20 specimens and exceeds the developmental null by at least 25 percentage points with a permutation p-value below 0.05.
approaches.failure_signature: Equivalent predictive accuracy of the two models, strong dependence on a tuned boundary condition, or failure on synthetic recovery falsifies the proposed discriminator.

references.note: Huiskes et al. 2000, Effects of mechanical forces on maintenance and adaptation of form in trabecular bone

approaches.missing: A public set of at least 20 specimens with known loading class is not yet established; static architecture cannot directly test reorientation after altered loading.

approaches.title: Measurement-aware leave-family-out toughness meta-analysis
approaches.method: Build a provenance-locked table of at least 40 records from nacre, cortical bone, dentin, antler and one additional mineralized composite. Record crack orientation, specimen dimensions, toughness protocol, hydration, mineral fraction, constituent moduli and strengths, platelet or fibril aspect ratio, interface compliance and a rule-based count of hierarchical levels. Fit a constituent-only mixing-law baseline and a hierarchical model with protocol-specific measurement error; test architecture by leave-one-family-out prediction rather than in-sample significance.
steps: Publish an extraction codebook and dual-extract a 20% paper sample before resolving disagreements.
Convert toughness measures only where standards make them commensurable; otherwise model protocol strata separately.
Fit constituent-only, descriptor and hierarchy-count models with family-level random effects.
Run leave-one-family-out prediction and a monotonicity test for hierarchy count.
approaches.decisive_result: Architecture explains a dataset-wide effect if the descriptor model reduces held-out log-toughness RMSE by at least 20% versus the constituent-only model in at least four of five held-out families; compounding requires a positive hierarchy-count coefficient whose 95% interval excludes zero after all controls.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than 40 commensurable records, no held-out RMSE gain, or a hierarchy-count interval containing zero defeats the corresponding claim.

datasets.name: Published biocomposite property records
datasets.note: Paper tables and supplements, retained only with specimen, hydration and fracture-protocol provenance.

references.note: Wegst et al. 2015, Bioinspired structural materials
Barthelat et al. 2016, Structure and mechanics of interfaces in biological materials

approaches.missing: The records are scattered and fracture-toughness protocols are heterogeneous; enough commensurable open records may not survive the exclusion rules.

approaches.title: Factorial fracture simulation isolates hierarchy from constituents
approaches.method: Construct a two-dimensional discrete cohesive-zone model with identical mineral fraction, constituent elastic laws and interface fracture energy across designs. Enumerate single-level brick-and-mortar, two-level nested and three-level nested architectures over platelet aspect ratio and interface-compliance grids. Match total mass and smallest feature size, compute J-integral or work-to-failure under mode-I and mixed-mode loading, and use a factorial decomposition to estimate the pure hierarchy interaction after controlling for tortuosity and interface area.
steps: Validate the solver against analytic laminate and single-crack limits.
Generate matched architectures over a preregistered parameter grid with mesh-convergence checks.
Compute peak stress, work-to-failure and crack-path tortuosity under two loading modes.
Fit a response surface and locate regions where adding a level helps, harms or is neutral.
approaches.decisive_result: Hierarchy compounds toughness in the model only if each added level raises median work-to-failure by at least 25% at fixed constituents, mass, interface area and minimum feature size across at least 75% of the preregistered parameter grid.
approaches.failure_signature: No mesh-converged gain, gains attributable entirely to extra interface area, or frequent decreases after adding levels refutes a generic hierarchy effect in this model class.

references.note: Wegst et al. 2015, Bioinspired structural materials

approaches.missing: This settles a controlled theoretical piece, not whether real tissues occupy the beneficial parameter region; three-dimensional validation would require more compute and measurements.

approaches.title: Formal Pareto envelope for hollow tubes with buckling constraints
approaches.method: State the circular-annulus optimization exactly: for fixed material area and length, derive second moment of area as a function of outer and inner radii, then add local shell buckling, Euler buckling and maximum-radius constraints. Prove in Lean 4 that unconstrained bending stiffness increases as material moves outward, that no finite wall-thickness optimum exists without an added constraint, and that the constrained optimum lies on at least one active buckling or radius boundary. Numerically map the resulting nondimensional Pareto envelope in slenderness, modulus and load.
steps: Define annular area, second moment, bending stiffness and nondimensional geometry in Lean.
Prove monotonicity at fixed area and existence of a constrained maximizer on a compact feasible set.
Prove the active-constraint lemma and verify symbolic special cases.
Generate a numerical envelope that converts measured radius, thickness and load into optimality gap.
approaches.decisive_result: A no-sorry Lean module proving the monotonicity, existence and active-constraint lemmas, plus a reproducible envelope, settles what 'stiffness-per-mass optimum' can mathematically mean and shows whether buckling is required to define a finite optimum.
approaches.failure_signature: A counterexample to the active-constraint lemma or an unavoidable unsupported shell-buckling axiom means the formal route has not established the claimed optimum.

references.note: Gibson, Ashby, Wegst and Olive 1995, The mechanical properties of natural materials II: Microstructures for mechanical efficiency

approaches.title: Cross-structure distance to the constrained tube optimum
approaches.method: Measure outer radius, wall-thickness distribution, length and ovality from at least 100 published cross-sections spanning long bones, bamboo or grass culms, stems and feather rachises. Use modulus and failure-property values from the same specimen or narrowly matched tissue, propagate those uncertainties through the formal Pareto envelope, and estimate each structure's log-distance from bending-optimal, local-buckling and Euler-buckling boundaries. Pre-register structure type, body size and safety factor as predictors in a hierarchical model.
steps: Scout records and freeze matching rules for geometry, material properties and loads.
Segment cross-sections with blinded duplicate measurements on 10% of records.
Compute uncertainty distributions over the three candidate constraint boundaries.
Fit type-specific and allometric models and perform leave-one-type-out validation.
approaches.decisive_result: A constraint explains a structure type if at least 70% of its records lie within 20% of that boundary and are at least twice as far from each competing boundary; otherwise that type is not classified as mechanically optimal under the model.
approaches.failure_signature: Insufficient matched material properties, no concentration near any boundary, or classification reversal under plausible loads refutes the cross-taxon optimum claim.

datasets.name: Published tube cross-sections and open CT
datasets.note: Only records with specimen-level geometry and same-specimen or narrowly matched tissue properties are admissible.

references.note: Gibson, Ashby, Wegst and Olive 1995, The mechanical properties of natural materials II: Microstructures for mechanical efficiency

approaches.missing: Same-specimen loads and tissue moduli are uncommon, especially for feathers and plants, and may reduce the admissible sample below 100.

approaches.title: Preregistered phylogenetic model contest for limb-bone scaling
approaches.method: Reanalyse the Campione and Evans quadruped measurements and an independently curated compilation, resolving taxa through the organisms layer. For circumference, cross-sectional area and section modulus separately, fit phylogenetic generalized least squares and multilevel models with bone, clade and posture interactions. Compare point hypotheses for area exponents 2/3, 3/4 and 1 using a predeclared equivalence margin of 0.04, while estimating phylogenetic uncertainty over a tree ensemble rather than one tree.
steps: Vendor measurements, body masses, posture classes and a dated tree ensemble with provenance.
Freeze exclusion, log transformation, equivalence margin and outlier rules.
Fit pooled and clade-by-bone models and test heterogeneity before selecting a universal exponent.
Validate on the independent compilation and report prediction intervals, not only coefficients.
approaches.decisive_result: A universal law is accepted only if the pooled exponent is within 0.04 of one candidate, the 95% interval excludes the other two margins, clade standard deviation is below 0.04, and the independent dataset reproduces that classification; otherwise universality is rejected.
approaches.failure_signature: Failure to reproduce the exponent independently, clade heterogeneity at least 0.04, or intervals overlapping multiple hypotheses defeats a single similarity law.

datasets.name: Campione and Evans 2012 supplementary data
datasets.note: Proximal humerus and femur circumference, body mass and locomotor grouping.

references.note: Campione and Evans 2012, A universal scaling relationship between body mass and proximal limb bone dimensions in quadrupedal terrestrial tetrapods

approaches.missing: An independent compilation with comparable posture metadata must be located; circumference alone does not identify safety factor.

approaches.title: Mechanistic safety-factor scaling with posture compensation
approaches.method: For a mammal subset with force-plate or published peak ground-reaction forces, combine body mass, limb effective mechanical advantage, bone length and CT-derived section modulus to estimate peak bending plus axial stress and safety factor. Fit two causal models: geometry-only similarity and posture-compensated stress similarity. Use measurement-error propagation and leave-clade-out prediction; the target is whether nearly flat safety factors arise only after posture is included.
steps: Scout at least 40 species with matchable gait force, posture and limb geometry records.
Pre-register load decomposition, muscle-force bounds and admissible taxonomic matching.
Estimate stress and safety-factor allometry with and without posture.
Test predictions in a held-out clade and conduct sensitivity analysis over material strength.
approaches.decisive_result: Posture compensation is supported if the mass slope of log safety factor has absolute value below 0.05 only in the posture model, and that model lowers held-out stress RMSE by at least 20% relative to geometry-only similarity.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than 40 matched species, a non-flat safety-factor slope after posture, or no predictive gain means the approach fails to explain scaling by mechanical similarity.

datasets.name: Published mammalian locomotor force and limb-geometry records
datasets.note: Species are admissible only when posture and geometry can be matched without genus-level substitution.

references.note: Biewener 1989, Scaling body support in mammals: limb posture and muscle mechanics

approaches.missing: The necessary force, posture, CT geometry and material-strength measurements are not known to coexist publicly for 40 species.

approaches.title: Independent-parameter audit of plant bilayer predictions
approaches.method: Extract specimen-level or reconstructable measurements for at least 20 hygromorphs from five species: layer thicknesses, orthotropic moduli, free swelling strains, moisture diffusivity, curvature-time traces and humidity step. Predict equilibrium curvature with the Timoshenko bilayer formula and response time with the first diffusion eigenmode without fitting either outcome. Pre-register error tolerances, digitization uncertainty and a graded orthotropic alternative, then use leave-species-out prediction to prevent species-specific calibration.
steps: Scout papers and supplements for jointly reported inputs and outcomes.
Dual-digitize figures and reject records lacking independently measured inputs.
Compute parameter-free bilayer predictions and uncertainty intervals.
Compare simple, orthotropic and viscoelastic models by leave-species-out predictive error.
approaches.decisive_result: The simple scaling passes if at least 16 of 20 equilibrium curvatures are within 25% of prediction and the fitted log response-time versus log thickness slope is within 0.25 of 2 with a 95% interval; otherwise report which extension achieves at least a 20% held-out error reduction.
approaches.failure_signature: Fewer than 20 jointly parameterized specimens, systematic curvature error above 25%, or a response-time slope interval excluding 2 by more than 0.25 refutes the simple model for the assembled species.

datasets.name: Published plant hygromorph measurements
datasets.note: Only records with independently measured thickness, swelling or diffusivity and an observed outcome are admissible.

references.note: Reyssat and Mahadevan 2009, Hygromorphs: from pine cones to biomimetic bilayers

approaches.missing: Published papers may not expose enough specimen-level combinations of moduli, swelling mismatch, diffusivity and time courses to reach 20 records.

approaches.title: Identifiability map for bilayer, graded and viscoelastic hygromorphs
approaches.method: Implement finite-element models for a sharp isotropic bilayer, an orthotropic bilayer, a continuous stiffness/swelling gradient and a viscoelastic bilayer. Sweep thickness ratio, modulus ratio, fibre angle, Biot number and relaxation-to-diffusion time ratio, then create synthetic curvature-time traces with realistic noise. Fit all four models blind to determine when curvature and response time can distinguish the simple law from its extensions and which additional observable is required when they cannot.
steps: Verify the simple solver against the existing bilayer curvature and diffusion limits.
Run a Latin-hypercube sweep with mesh and time-step convergence.
Perform blinded model recovery from synthetic traces.
Publish a decision map and minimal measurement design for future specimens.
approaches.decisive_result: The approach succeeds with a reproducible map identifying parameter regions where the true model is recovered with at least 90% accuracy and a ranked extra observable, such as through-thickness strain or relaxation after humidity reversal, for non-identifiable regions.
approaches.failure_signature: Failure to recover even the generating model under low noise, or universal non-identifiability across the sweep, shows curvature-time data cannot test the proposed deviations.

references.note: Reyssat and Mahadevan 2009, Hygromorphs: from pine cones to biomimetic bilayers

approaches.missing: The result designs and validates a discriminator but does not supply new biological measurements.

approaches.title: Spherical-lattice geometry contest across mineral classes
approaches.method: Assemble at least 30 calibrated, near-orthographic SEM or optical images spanning silica radiolarians, strontium-sulphate acantharians and organic Clathrulina-like lattices, with at least eight specimens per material class. Segment vertices and edges blind to material, correct spherical projection where possible, and measure polygon-side counts, vertex angles, edge-length coefficient of variation and topological defects. Compare a noisy equal-area foam model, a spherical Poisson-Voronoi null and a phylogenetically structured material model using held-out image likelihood.
steps: Scout images with taxon, scale and composition provenance and freeze inclusion criteria.
Validate segmentation against duplicate manual annotations on 20% of images.
Simulate matched-size foam and random-Voronoi nulls on the sphere.
Fit material and phylogenetic effects and perform leave-taxon-out prediction.
approaches.decisive_result: Packing physics is supported for mature geometry if the foam model improves held-out log predictive density over random Voronoi in all three materials and material class explains under 5% additional variance; a material effect above 20% refutes mineral independence.
approaches.failure_signature: No advantage over random Voronoi, segmentation error comparable to model differences, or fewer than eight usable specimens in any material class defeats this comparison.

datasets.name: Open protist lattice-shell image archives
datasets.note: Images require specimen identity, scale and mineral-class provenance; historical drawings are excluded from the primary analysis.

references.note: Weiner and Addadi 2011, Crystallization pathways in biomineralization

approaches.missing: The availability and licensing of enough calibrated acantharian and organic-lattice SEM images are uncertain; mature images cannot establish the developmental vesicle mechanism.

approaches.title: Morphology fingerprints of templating versus self-organization
approaches.method: Generate preregistered morphology fingerprints for three mechanisms on a curved surface: equal-area vesicle packing with deposition in interfaces, Cahn-Hilliard phase separation with mineral precipitation, and an explicit cell-template field with controlled spatial correlations. Match only area fraction and mean spacing, then compare higher-order observables that were not fitted: defect charge versus curvature, three-point correlations, edge-width distribution and concentric-layer registration. Apply the frozen classifier to the image set from the geometry test.
steps: Implement and convergence-test all three mechanism classes on identical spherical meshes.
Generate a balanced simulation library over nuisance parameters.
Train a classifier on simulations using only preregistered higher-order observables.
Run simulation-based calibration and then classify biological images with an abstention threshold.
approaches.decisive_result: A bounded mechanism is distinguished if synthetic held-out accuracy exceeds 90% and at least 70% of biological images receive posterior probability above 0.8 for one class; otherwise the tested morphology is non-identifying.
approaches.failure_signature: Synthetic mechanisms overlap after matching area fraction and spacing, classifier calibration fails, or biological images mostly trigger abstention, showing geometry alone cannot separate control modes.

references.note: Politi et al. 2004, Sea urchin spine calcite forms via a transient amorphous calcium carbonate phase

approaches.missing: This can reject morphological sufficiency but cannot prove cellular control without developmental imaging or perturbation data.

approaches.title: Robust virtual tournament of aligned and uniform lattices
approaches.method: Define three load cases and generate paired stress-aligned and uniform lattices with equal mass, strut count, bounding volume and minimum printable diameter. Evaluate nonlinear finite-element failure under resin-like elastic-plastic and brittle laws while sampling print-realistic diameter error, missing struts, anisotropy and load misalignment. Include a topology-optimized positive control so failure of the aligned design can be separated from failure of the solver or design space.
steps: Freeze geometry-matching and load definitions and verify mesh convergence.
Generate at least 100 matched design pairs per load case.
Sample at least 1,000 manufacturing-error realizations per pair using preregistered distributions.
Compare peak load and absorbed energy with hierarchical paired effects and worst-decile performance.
approaches.decisive_result: A robust virtual advantage requires at least 20% higher median peak load or energy and a positive paired effect in the worst decile for every load case; topology optimization must beat or match both as a solver sanity check.
approaches.failure_signature: An advantage that vanishes under modest load misalignment or diameter noise, reverses for a load case, or depends on unequal feature size refutes general robust superiority in simulation.

references.note: Aage, Andreassen, Lazarov and Sigmund 2017, Giga-voxel computational morphogenesis for structural design
Sigmund, Aage and Andreassen 2016, On the non-optimality of Michell structures

approaches.missing: The assumed defect and resin models need eventual calibration against a real printer; this approach settles only the computational robustness claim.

approaches.title: Partner-ready blinded print-and-failure protocol
approaches.method: Prepare production files and a sealed preregistration for 10 stress-aligned and 10 uniform specimens per each of three load cases, plus five solid calibration coupons per print batch. Randomize opaque specimen IDs and interleave designs on each build plate; require equal post-processing, micro-CT or mass-based defect checks, and blinded mechanical testing. Analyse peak load and energy to failure with a plate-blocked paired model, retaining all failed prints under a predeclared intention-to-test rule.
steps: Use the virtual tournament to lock geometries, tolerances, effect threshold and power calculation.
Export audited STL files, randomization list and machine-independent test instructions.
Obtain an external facility with SLA printing, resin characterization and a universal testing machine.
Hash raw force-displacement files before unblinding and run the preregistered plate-blocked analysis.
approaches.decisive_result: The printed claim passes only if the aligned design exceeds uniform by at least 20% in either peak load or energy to failure, with a 95% interval above zero, in all three load cases and the gain exceeds twice the within-design print coefficient of variation.
approaches.failure_signature: No facility, fewer than 10 valid replicates per design-case cell, a gain below variability, or a reversed ranking in any load case leaves or refutes the general printed advantage.

references.note: Aage, Andreassen, Lazarov and Sigmund 2017, Giga-voxel computational morphogenesis for structural design

approaches.missing: The swarm has no printer, resin, universal testing machine, post-processing line or laboratory partner; completing the physical experiment within a month depends entirely on external access.
